Hi Alex — great to meet this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps after our discovery: 

What I heard:
- Use case: interactive financial assistant embedded in customer dashboard (many short prompts, some longer follow-ups).
- Target users: ~200k MAU in year 1; estimated 5-10 prompts/user/day (avg 75 tokens/prompt); rough starting volume: 700M-1.5B tokens/month.
- Latency expectation: interactive experience — aiming for p95 latency in the sub-300ms range for core flows; some background async tasks can be higher.
- Budget: initial pilot budget estimate ~$20k–$60k/month; looking for unit economics that scale to CA$ per 1M tokens targets (we discussed $/1M targets).

Open questions / confirmations needed:
1) Can you confirm the upper bound of monthly token volume (best effort)?
2) Which flows are strictly interactive (need p95 <300ms) vs background?
3) Procurement timeline (Sabrina?) and any PO/contract constraints we should know.

Attachment: I’m sending a pricing sheet and draft pilot SOW for a ballpark estimate. In short, we typically recommend starting on a hosted plan to iterate on prompts and then moving to a dedicated pool if committed throughput warrants lower unit cost.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm volumes + SLOs (reply inline) — I’ll update the pricing estimates.
- Rishi to run a latency vs cost options doc (tech tradeoffs: streaming vs batching, quantization, SLO tiers).
- Tentative technical deep-dive next week to map SLOs to tier choices and estimate $/1M tokens.

Thanks — attaching the pricing sheet and SOW.

Thanks Marissa — very helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: 700M-1.5B tokens/month is a reasonable working estimate, but month 1 will be much smaller (pilot: ~40-60M tokens) as we test with a closed beta. If the beta performs well we expect a 6-9 month ramp.
- Interactive vs background: ~80% of our calls will be interactive (dashboard prompts, quick clarifications). The remaining 20% are async batch jobs (overnight enrichment).
- Budget: for pilot we have flexibility up to $25k; for production we’re targeting sub-$1,200 per 1M tokens ideally, but that’s negotiable depending on latency guarantees and support.

Specific questions:
1) Can you share a short example of how latency SLO tiers map to unit cost? E.g., if we want p95 <300ms for interactive flows, what delta should we expect vs a 600ms SLO?
2) For streaming vs batching: is streaming materially more expensive when you have a lot of small prompts? Any rule of thumb?
3) If we commit to a 12-month Dedicated pool, what ballpark $/1M tokens could we expect?

Alex — thanks for the clarity. Below is a concise breakdown tying SLOs and deployment tiers to approximate unit economics. These are ballpark figures to help with qualification; Rishi will follow up with technical tradeoffs next.

High-level unit economics (approx, hosted prices):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) — typical for pilot
  - Default (streaming enabled, standard model): ~$1,200 per 1M tokens
  - With aggressive batching/CKV cache for prefix-heavy workloads: ~$900 per 1M tokens (best-effort on latency)

- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool — 12mo commit) — recommended when sustained volume > ~400M tokens/month
  - Baseline dedicated (quantized model variants, optimized kernels): ~$400–$600 per 1M tokens
  - Optimized dedicated (larger commit, aggressive quantization + model distill): ~$250–$350 per 1M tokens

SLO-driven deltas (interactive p95 examples):
- p95 target ~300ms (tight interactive): typically requires smaller batch sizes, faster GPUs, and streaming-friendly configs => expect +20–40% on unit cost vs looser SLOs.
- p95 target ~600ms (relaxed): allows larger batching and higher throughput paths => unit cost can be 15–30% lower than the tight SLO case.

Streaming vs batching (rule-of-thumb):
- Streaming gives best UX for long-turn interactions and predictable tail latency but reduces batching efficiency on many small prompts; cost impact depends on average prompt length. For many short prompts (like your 75-token average), batching + streaming hybrid (stream first token then batch later tokens) can save 10–30% relative to pure streaming.

Operational levers to reduce $/1M tokens without breaking latency:
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated user context (can cut token compute by ~15–40% on session-heavy apps).
- Model selection & quantization for background flows (use lower-cost variants for async jobs).
- Commitment (Dedicated) + autoscaling windows for peak vs off-peak traffic.

Pilot recommendation (based on your numbers & $25k pilot budget):
- Start hosted API with streaming enabled for interactive flows + KV caching enabled.
- Measure real p95 and token distribution over the 30-day beta.
- If steady-state looks like >400M tokens/mo, migrate to a 12mo Dedicated commit and target the $250–$400 per 1M tokens range with quantized variants and batching.

Next steps:

- Rishi — can you add a short tech note on batching/tuning options and propose an SE deep-dive slot?
- Alex/Sabrina — if you can confirm the pilot window and internal approvers, I’ll get a draft PO path ready.

Thanks — happy to walk through numbers on a quick call.

+1 on Marissa’s recommendations. A couple of technical notes and a proposed agenda for our SE deep-dive: 

Technical notes (short):
- For p95 <300ms we generally recommend: 1) low-latency GPU instances, 2) small micro-batches (batch window ~5–10ms), 3) streaming first-token then batch remaining where possible, and 4) KV caches for session state. Expect 20–40% higher CPU/GPU utilization vs relaxed SLOs.
- Batching efficiency: if you can tolerate p95 ~600ms for non-critical flows, we can increase batch windows and reduce per-token cost ~15–30%.
- Quantization: INT8/4 can reduce memory/compute and lower cost, but test for quality regressions on your prompts. Background/async jobs are ideal candidates.

Proposed SE deep-dive agenda (30–45m):
1) Walk through critical interactive flows (identify which user flows need p95 <300ms).
2) Run a simple cost projection using your real sample traces (we’ll need a small sample CSV of request lengths/timestamps).
3) Map SLOs to tier choices and estimate expected $/1M tokens under streaming vs batch.
4) Next steps: pilot instrumentation and performance gating.

I’m available Wed Mar 17 11:00–11:45 PT or Thu Mar 18 09:00–09:45 PT. Alex — which works for your team? If you can also share a small sample of request telemetry (anonymized), we’ll prepare the cost model before the call.
